title: India's Spending Abroad: Understanding the Current Account Deficit
description: India's Current Account Deficit (CAD) widened to $7 billion in July 2026. This means India spent more foreign currency than it earned from trade and other tra.

faq.q: What are the main reasons for India's CAD widening in July 2026?
faq.a: The primary reason for the widening of India's Current Account Deficit in July 2026 was a larger merchandise trade deficit, meaning the value of goods imported by India significantly exceeded the value of goods exported.

faq.q: How does the RBI address a widening CAD?
faq.a: The RBI monitors the CAD closely and can take various measures to manage it. These might include encouraging foreign investment, managing interest rates, or intervening in the foreign exchange market to stabilise the rupee.

faq.q: Is India's CAD always in deficit?
faq.a: No, India has experienced periods of Current Account Surplus as well, though a deficit has been more common in recent years. For example, India recorded a current account surplus in Q1 FY21 (April-June 2020) during the initial phase of the pandemic.

faq.q: What is the difference between Current Account and Capital Account?
faq.a: The Current Account records transactions related to goods, services, income, and transfers. The Capital Account, on the other hand, records international capital transfers and financial transactions like foreign direct investment (FDI), foreign portfolio investment (FPI), and external borrowings.
The Current Account Deficit is typically measured in US dollars and also expressed as a percentage of a country's Gross Domestic Product (GDP) to show its size relative to the economy.
